terms.plain_language: The part of the product that turns verified business and search data into prioritized next steps.
terms.technical_definition: A deterministic pipeline that assembles facts, evaluates governed rules, records evidence, creates allowed recommendations, and supplies bounded context to an AI narrative layer.

terms.plain_language: A measured fact the system can use.
terms.technical_definition: A typed, sourced, time-bound observation at page, origin, location, campaign, organization, or portfolio scope.

terms.plain_language: A consistent way to measure performance.
terms.technical_definition: A governed calculation with units, aggregation, scope, freshness, provenance, and optional thresholds.

terms.plain_language: A specific problem the verified data supports.
terms.technical_definition: A deterministic classification produced only when required evidence and rule conditions are satisfied.

terms.plain_language: A next step connected to a verified problem and a measurable result.
terms.technical_definition: A versioned action reference carrying evidence, confidence, effort, risk, owner, success metrics, and an observation window.

terms.plain_language: How complete and reliable the evidence is for this recommendation.
terms.technical_definition: A calibrated evidence-quality score, not a probability that a ranking or revenue outcome will occur.

terms.plain_language: How much control and approval an action needs.
terms.technical_definition: Tier 0 is insight only, Tier 1 is draft only, Tier 2 is low-risk publish, Tier 3 is high-risk publish requiring approval, and Tier 4 is structural change requiring a governed code or configuration change.

terms.plain_language: How long to wait before judging whether an action helped.
terms.technical_definition: A predefined interval between an action baseline and an outcome measurement.

terms.plain_language: Performance measured from real Chrome visits over time.
terms.technical_definition: Aggregated Chrome UX Report observations, typically a rolling 28-day distribution reported at URL or origin scope.

terms.plain_language: A controlled performance test useful for finding likely causes.
terms.technical_definition: A Lighthouse-style synthetic run under defined device and network conditions; useful for diagnostics but not a substitute for field data.

terms.plain_language: Google's three real-user measures for loading, responsiveness, and visual stability.
terms.technical_definition: The current set of LCP, INP, and CLS, assessed at the 75th percentile; all three must be good for the set to pass.

terms.plain_language: The product does not have enough reliable information to make this decision.
terms.technical_definition: A first-class state that blocks deterministic classification when required facts are absent, stale, or below provider coverage requirements.

terms.plain_language: A claim that one action directly produced a result.
terms.technical_definition: A statement requiring governed experimentation and sufficient evidence; ordinary before-and-after comparisons remain observational.

metrics.plain_language: How quickly the main visible content loads.
metrics.caveat: Assess field data at p75. URL data can fall back to origin data only when the fallback is labeled.

metrics.plain_language: How quickly the page responds when someone uses it.
metrics.caveat: INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024.

metrics.plain_language: How stable the page stays while it loads.
metrics.caveat: CrUX encodes CLS percentile values as decimal strings; consumers must normalize them without changing precision.

metrics.plain_language: How quickly the server begins responding.
metrics.caveat: TTFB is a supporting diagnostic and is not a Core Web Vital.

metrics.plain_language: The share of search appearances that became clicks.
metrics.caveat: The boundaries are internal diagnostic defaults. CTR varies materially by query intent, position, search feature, brand demand, device, and market; do not present them as Google thresholds.

metrics.plain_language: The number of times the business appeared in Google Search.
metrics.caveat: The boundary is an internal minimum-evidence default and must be calibrated to the selected date range and scope.

metrics.plain_language: The click-rate difference between the business and a comparable competitor estimate.
metrics.caveat: This is an internal comparison threshold. Estimated competitor CTR must always remain labeled as estimated.

metrics.plain_language: Average position in the selected Search Console or rank-tracking scope.
metrics.caveat: Average position is contextual and should not be treated as a universal score.

metrics.plain_language: The change in average position from the comparison period.
metrics.caveat: An internal alert boundary; positive and negative sign conventions must be normalized before evaluation.

metrics.plain_language: Change in organic visits from the comparison period.
metrics.caveat: An internal change classification, not a Google standard.

metrics.plain_language: The number of reviews added in the last 30 days.
metrics.caveat: The numerical boundary is an internal operating heuristic and should be calibrated by industry and location.

metrics.plain_language: How many times this location appeared on Google Search and Maps during the saved period.
metrics.caveat: This measures provider-reported appearances for one connected location and date window; it is not a ranking score.

metrics.display_name: Website visits from your Google profile
metrics.plain_language: Clicks from this location's Google profile to its website during the saved period.
metrics.caveat: This counts provider-reported profile clicks and does not prove a sale or lead.

metrics.display_name: Call clicks from your Google profile
metrics.plain_language: Clicks on the call button for this location during the saved period.
metrics.caveat: This counts supported call-button clicks and does not confirm a completed phone call.

metrics.display_name: Direction requests from your Google profile
metrics.plain_language: Requests for directions to this location during the saved period.
metrics.caveat: This counts provider-reported direction requests and does not confirm an in-person visit.

metrics.plain_language: Booking actions reported for this location during the saved period.
metrics.caveat: Availability depends on the connected profile and booking setup.

metrics.plain_language: The share of reviews answered by the business.
metrics.caveat: The numerical boundary is an internal service-level goal, not a Google ranking threshold.

metrics.plain_language: How far the business trails comparison businesses in review count.
metrics.caveat: Calibrate by market, category, and competitor set.

metrics.plain_language: Average public rating for the location.
metrics.caveat: Interpret relative to rating distribution, review recency, volume, and the local competitor set.

metrics.plain_language: How far the business rating trails selected competitors.
metrics.caveat: Internal comparison boundary, not a Google standard.

metrics.plain_language: How far the business trails selected competitors in average ranking position.
metrics.caveat: Internal comparison boundary; use the same queries, location, device, and collection window.

metrics.plain_language: Technical issues relative to the number of pages checked.
metrics.caveat: Severity and affected templates matter more than raw count alone.

metrics.plain_language: The share of crawled pages receiving internal-link support.
metrics.caveat: Internal heuristic; page purpose and site architecture must remain part of review.

metrics.plain_language: A product heuristic based on the density of stored technical issues.
metrics.caveat: Not a Google score and must always expose its component issues.

metrics.plain_language: How publishing output changed during the selected period.
metrics.caveat: More content is not automatically better; quality and customer usefulness remain required.

metrics.plain_language: The direction and speed of ranking movement.
metrics.caveat: Internal trend boundary; require enough observations and expose volatility.

metrics.display_name: Exact page links to your website
metrics.plain_language: Whether the exact outside page now links to this business website.
metrics.caveat: This verifies one exact page-to-site link observation. It does not prove a ranking or revenue change.

actions.display_name: Rewrite the page title and description for clearer search intent
actions.why_it_matters: A clearer result can earn more qualified clicks without requiring a higher ranking.
steps: Identify the queries and page with the CTR gap.
Rewrite the title and description around the service, location, and search intent.
Preview the result and obtain approval before publishing.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior title and description if relevance or qualified traffic declines.

actions.display_name: Match search-result wording to the customer's intent
actions.why_it_matters: People are more likely to click when the result clearly answers the service and location they searched for.
steps: Group the affected queries by intent.
Compare the page promise with the query modifiers.
Propose one intent-aligned revision for review.
actions.rollback_guidance: Discard the draft or restore the prior copy.

actions.display_name: Compare stronger search-result wording
actions.why_it_matters: A side-by-side review can reveal clearer offers or trust signals without copying competitors.
steps: Capture results for the same query, location, and device.
Compare clarity, service fit, location fit, and value proposition.
Draft differentiated improvements.
actions.rollback_guidance: Keep the comparison as research and publish nothing.

actions.display_name: Make the search result's value clearer
actions.why_it_matters: A specific, truthful reason to choose the business can improve qualified clicks.
steps: Identify the page's strongest verified value proposition.
Add it to the proposed title or description without unsupported claims.
Review for accuracy before publishing.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior metadata if qualified traffic worsens.

actions.display_name: Reduce files that delay the main content
actions.why_it_matters: Render-blocking scripts and styles can delay the content customers came to see.
steps: Use a current Lighthouse run to identify render-blocking resources.
Remove unused resources or defer noncritical work.
Retest in the lab, then monitor CrUX field data.
actions.rollback_guidance: Revert the asset-loading change if layout, tracking, or site functionality regresses.

actions.display_name: Improve the server's initial response time
actions.why_it_matters: A slow server delays every later loading step.
steps: Confirm TTFB in field and lab data.
Profile hosting, caching, redirects, and backend work.
Apply one controlled improvement and retest.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior cache, routing, or hosting configuration if errors or latency increase.

actions.display_name: Prioritize the page's main visible content
actions.why_it_matters: The browser should discover and load the largest above-the-fold element quickly.
steps: Identify the LCP element in a current lab run.
Optimize its format, size, discovery, and priority.
Retest lab data and monitor p75 CrUX data.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior resource markup if visual quality or rendering breaks.

actions.display_name: Reduce browser work that delays interactions
actions.why_it_matters: Long tasks can make taps and clicks feel unresponsive.
steps: Identify long tasks and heavy scripts in a current lab trace.
Remove, split, or defer nonessential work.
Retest interactions and monitor INP field data.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior script bundle if functionality or measurement breaks.

actions.display_name: Make important clicks and taps respond faster
actions.why_it_matters: Customers may abandon a page when forms, menus, or buttons respond slowly.
steps: Identify the slow interaction type.
Measure input delay, handler work, and presentation delay.
Reduce synchronous work and retest the interaction.
actions.rollback_guidance: Revert the handler change if the interaction becomes unreliable.

actions.display_name: Reserve space for images and embedded content
actions.why_it_matters: Reserved space prevents buttons and text from unexpectedly moving while customers use the page.
steps: Identify the elements contributing to layout shift.
Set stable dimensions or aspect ratios.
Retest on representative mobile and desktop layouts.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore prior styling if responsive layouts regress.

actions.display_name: Stop late content from moving the page
actions.why_it_matters: Unexpected movement causes misclicks and makes the page harder to use.
steps: Identify injected banners, fonts, ads, or widgets causing shifts.
Reserve space or change insertion behavior.
Retest across devices and monitor CLS field data.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the previous component behavior if content becomes inaccessible.

actions.display_name: Review the pages losing visibility
actions.why_it_matters: Focusing on the affected pages is more useful than making broad site-wide changes.
steps: List pages and query groups with verified decline.
Check intent, indexing, content changes, internal links, and competing results.
Choose the smallest evidence-backed correction.
actions.rollback_guidance: Keep the work as research until a specific change is approved.

actions.display_name: Refresh the affected service pages
actions.why_it_matters: A focused refresh can restore usefulness and intent alignment on pages with verified decline.
steps: Confirm the page and query evidence.
Update outdated or incomplete sections for customers.
Review and approve before publishing.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior approved copy if relevance or qualified traffic declines.

actions.display_name: Ask completed customers for reviews consistently
actions.why_it_matters: A consistent, policy-compliant request process helps the business build current social proof.
steps: Choose compliant post-service request moments.
Create a simple request template without incentives or review gating.
Track requests and resulting reviews by location.
actions.rollback_guidance: Pause the workflow and retain the prior request process if consent or policy issues appear.

actions.display_name: Reach more eligible completed customers
actions.why_it_matters: Gaps in the request process can leave many satisfied customers unasked.
steps: Measure the share of eligible customers receiving a request.
Find missed service-completion touchpoints.
Add approved requests without incentives or review gating.
actions.rollback_guidance: Remove the added touchpoint if consent, deliverability, or policy problems occur.

actions.display_name: Set a clear review-response routine
actions.why_it_matters: Consistent responses show customers that the business pays attention and resolves concerns.
steps: Assign an owner and response timeframe.
Use truthful, non-defensive response guidelines.
Review response coverage weekly.
actions.rollback_guidance: Revise the internal routine; do not delete valid public responses solely to reset the process.

actions.display_name: Clear unanswered reviews
actions.why_it_matters: A visible backlog can make the business appear inattentive.
steps: Sort unanswered reviews by recency and rating.
Draft factual, personalized responses.
Approve and publish through an authorized profile connection.
actions.rollback_guidance: Edit or remove a response through the provider when it contains an error or violates policy.

actions.display_name: Increase compliant review requests
actions.why_it_matters: A growing review footprint can narrow a visible trust gap with local competitors.
steps: Confirm the location-specific competitor gap.
Increase requests only among eligible completed customers.
Monitor review velocity and policy compliance.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return to the prior request cadence if quality, consent, or policy signals worsen.

actions.display_name: Focus review work on locations with the clearest gap
actions.why_it_matters: Location-specific effort avoids spreading the team too thin.
steps: Compare review gaps and business priority by location.
Select the smallest set of priority locations.
Track each location separately.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return locations to the normal operating cadence if prioritization is not useful.

actions.display_name: Reconnect competitor data
actions.why_it_matters: The product cannot make a trustworthy comparison without current competitor facts.
steps: Check connection health and permissions.
Confirm the selected competitors and location scope.
Run an idempotent backfill after access is restored.
actions.rollback_guidance: Disable the failing connection and retain the last verified snapshot as stale.

actions.display_name: Backfill missing competitor measurements
actions.why_it_matters: A complete comparison window is required before the system can prioritize competitive work.
steps: Identify missing dates, locations, and providers.
Estimate request cost before collection.
Run a bounded, idempotent backfill and verify coverage.
actions.rollback_guidance: Stop collection and discard invalid snapshots without overwriting verified history.

actions.display_name: Improve the service issues reflected in reviews
actions.why_it_matters: Better review outcomes begin with correcting recurring customer experience problems.
steps: Group verified review themes without exposing sensitive data.
Assign operational owners to recurring issues.
Measure whether new feedback improves after changes.
actions.rollback_guidance: Reassess the operational intervention if customer feedback does not improve.

actions.display_name: Resolve recurring negative feedback themes
actions.why_it_matters: Repeated complaints often identify a service problem that reputation tactics alone cannot fix.
steps: Validate that the theme recurs across multiple reviews.
Separate operational issues from isolated complaints.
Create and track a specific service correction.
actions.rollback_guidance: Stop or revise the intervention if it creates new customer friction.

actions.display_name: Improve pages with the largest verified ranking gap
actions.why_it_matters: Concentrating on the clearest page-level gaps creates a more measurable plan.
steps: Match the same query, location, device, and page type.
Compare customer usefulness and intent coverage.
Approve one focused page improvement.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore the prior approved page if relevance or qualified traffic declines.

actions.display_name: Strengthen intent coverage and internal-link support
actions.why_it_matters: A relevant page also needs clear site support so customers and crawlers can find it.
steps: Confirm the page answers the target service and location intent.
Identify relevant internal-link sources.
Draft content and link changes for approval.
actions.rollback_guidance: Remove the new links or restore prior content if navigation or relevance worsens.

actions.display_name: Prioritize the pages losing ground fastest
actions.why_it_matters: Negative momentum helps distinguish a current problem from ordinary ranking noise.
steps: Confirm enough observations and acceptable volatility.
Rank affected pages by business importance and decline strength.
Review the highest-priority page first.
actions.rollback_guidance: Keep the work as analysis until a specific page change is approved.

actions.display_name: Support declining service-topic groups
actions.why_it_matters: Related pages and internal links can be reviewed together when a whole service topic is weakening.
steps: Confirm the decline occurs across a coherent query cluster.
Audit intent coverage and internal-link paths.
Propose the smallest coordinated improvement.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore prior content or internal links if the cluster's relevance or navigation worsens.

actions.display_name: Restore the recent review pace
actions.why_it_matters: A slowing review pace can make the profile's social proof less current.
steps: Compare recent review pace with the location's own prior baseline.
Check whether the request workflow stopped reaching completed customers.
Restore compliant requests at the missing touchpoints.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return to the prior cadence if consent, deliverability, or policy issues appear.

actions.display_name: Add a compliant reminder for unanswered review requests
actions.why_it_matters: A single approved reminder can recover missed responses without pressuring customers.
steps: Confirm consent and channel rules.
Send no more than the approved reminder cadence.
Track opt-outs, delivery, and resulting reviews.
actions.rollback_guidance: Disable reminders immediately if consent, complaint, or deliverability signals worsen.

actions.display_name: Restore a realistic publishing cadence
actions.why_it_matters: A consistent plan helps the business complete useful pages instead of accumulating unfinished work.
steps: Confirm the decline in completed, useful content.
Set a sustainable cadence around customer needs and priority services.
Track completed and performing pages, not drafts alone.
actions.rollback_guidance: Reduce the cadence if quality, accuracy, or approval throughput declines.

actions.display_name: Move low-value ideas behind higher-priority customer needs
actions.why_it_matters: Publishing capacity should go to useful content connected to verified demand and business goals.
steps: Score backlog items by customer usefulness, evidence, and business priority.
Pause items without a clear audience or purpose.
Commit to the highest-value approved items.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore a paused item when new evidence supports it.

actions.display_name: Focus work on service topics where competitors are accelerating
actions.why_it_matters: The team can respond to the clearest competitive gap instead of making broad changes.
steps: Verify the competitor and query-cluster comparison.
Rank gaps by business importance and evidence quality.
Assign one bounded response.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return the cluster to normal monitoring if the comparison becomes stale or unstable.

actions.display_name: Choose the action with the strongest measured upside
actions.why_it_matters: Capacity should go to an action with clear evidence, manageable risk, and a measurable result.
steps: Compare allowed actions using evidence, effort, risk, and success metric coverage.
Select one action without inventing an outcome forecast.
Record a baseline before work begins.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return to the prior priority order if evidence quality changes.

actions.display_name: Use smaller tests while rankings are volatile
actions.why_it_matters: Small changes are easier to evaluate when the market is moving unpredictably.
steps: Confirm volatility across enough observations.
Choose one page, location, or cluster.
Change one governed variable and record the baseline.
actions.rollback_guidance: End the test and restore the baseline when the result is unclear or harmful.

actions.display_name: Review volatile results more frequently
actions.why_it_matters: A shorter review interval can detect instability without triggering broad reactive changes.
steps: Set a temporary review cadence.
Keep collection definitions unchanged.
Do not publish new changes until the evidence stabilizes.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return to the normal review cadence when volatility settles.

actions.display_name: Add relevant internal links
actions.why_it_matters: Relevant links help customers and crawlers discover important service pages.
steps: Identify pages with weak internal-link support.
Choose relevant source pages and descriptive link text.
Review and approve links before publishing.
actions.rollback_guidance: Remove links that harm clarity or navigation.

actions.display_name: Review site navigation links
actions.why_it_matters: Important service and location pages should be easy for customers to reach.
steps: Map current navigation paths.
Find important pages requiring excessive steps.
Propose a small navigation correction.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore prior navigation if usability or conversion paths worsen.

actions.display_name: Refresh declining pages
actions.why_it_matters: Focused updates can restore customer usefulness on pages with verified decline.
steps: Verify the affected page and query evidence.
Update outdated or incomplete information.
Approve before publishing and measure afterward.
actions.rollback_guidance: Restore prior approved content if qualified performance worsens.

actions.display_name: Add useful supporting coverage
actions.why_it_matters: Customers may need related answers before choosing a service.
steps: Identify a verified information gap around the affected service.
Create only content that serves a clear customer need.
Connect it to the appropriate service page.
actions.rollback_guidance: Unpublish or revise content that is inaccurate, redundant, or unhelpful.

actions.display_name: Increase completion of useful content
actions.why_it_matters: A sustainable completion rate prevents high-priority customer questions from remaining unanswered.
steps: Measure approved content completed, not drafts started.
Remove workflow blockers.
Increase cadence only while quality remains stable.
actions.rollback_guidance: Return to the prior cadence if quality or approval performance declines.

actions.display_name: Publish approved supporting service-topic pages
actions.why_it_matters: Helpful supporting pages can answer customer questions and strengthen a coherent service topic.
steps: Confirm each page has a distinct customer purpose.
Review accuracy and avoid duplicate intent.
Approve, publish, and connect the page within the site.
actions.rollback_guidance: Unpublish or consolidate pages that duplicate intent or fail quality review.

actions.display_name: Ask for one useful website mention
actions.why_it_matters: A relevant page that already helps customers find similar businesses may also be a sensible place to mention this business.
steps: Open the exact page and confirm it serves the same customers.
Identify a truthful partnership, resource, or business mention that would help the page's visitors.
Contact the page owner without buying, trading, or demanding a link.
Run a fresh website-mention check after the follow-up.
actions.rollback_guidance: Close the action without making a website change if the page is not relevant or the site owner declines.

actions.display_name: Restore one useful website mention
actions.why_it_matters: A page that previously linked to the business may have an outdated destination or a removable mistake worth correcting.
steps: Open the exact source page and the former destination.
Confirm the mention still belongs there and choose the most useful current business page.
Ask the site owner to restore or update the link.
Run a fresh website-mention check after the follow-up.
actions.rollback_guidance: Close the action if the mention no longer belongs on the page; no business website change is required.

diagnostics.business_label: People see the business but do not click often enough
diagnostics.diagnosis: Search visibility is strong enough to evaluate, but the observed click rate is weak for the current context.
root_cause_hypotheses: The search-result wording does not clearly match the query intent.
The result lacks a specific, verified value proposition.
Search features or stronger competing results may be absorbing clicks.
evidence_requirements: Use the same date range and Search Console dimensions.
Require enough impressions before classifying the gap.
Compare by query, page, device, and brand/non-brand context where available.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: A measurable improvement in qualified CTR at comparable visibility.

diagnostics.business_label: Competing search results appear more compelling
diagnostics.diagnosis: The business has a verified CTR gap against comparable competitor visibility.
root_cause_hypotheses: Competitor wording may communicate the service or value more clearly.
The business result may be less aligned with local intent.
evidence_requirements: Label competitor CTR as observed or estimated.
Compare equivalent queries, positions, locations, and devices.
Do not infer the competitor's conversion quality.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: A narrower observed CTR gap without unsupported ranking claims.

diagnostics.business_label: Real users are experiencing a slow or unstable page
diagnostics.diagnosis: At least one of LCP, INP, or CLS is not good at the 75th percentile.
root_cause_hypotheses: The main content may be discovered or delivered too slowly.
Browser main-thread work may delay interactions.
Images, fonts, embeds, or dynamic components may move the layout.
evidence_requirements: Require p75 field data for LCP, INP, and CLS.
Keep mobile, desktop, URL, and origin scopes explicit.
Label origin fallback and insufficient data.
Use lab data to investigate causes, not to replace field truth.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: All three Core Web Vitals reach good p75 field-data status for the evaluated scope.

diagnostics.diagnosis: Ranking decline is supported by a related traffic or visibility loss.
root_cause_hypotheses: Affected pages may no longer match search intent as well.
Competitors or search-result composition may have changed.
Technical, indexing, or internal-link support may have weakened.
evidence_requirements: Require a stable comparison window.
Separate location and keyword clusters.
Do not treat normal volatility as a confirmed decline.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: The affected pages stabilize or recover without broad unsupported changes.

diagnostics.business_label: The location is receiving too few new reviews
diagnostics.diagnosis: The recent review pace is below the governed location target.
root_cause_hypotheses: Completed customers may not consistently receive a request.
The request may arrive at the wrong time or through the wrong channel.
The current target may need industry and location calibration.
evidence_requirements: Use a location-specific rolling window.
Show the internal target and prior baseline.
Do not represent the product threshold as a Google ranking standard.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: A policy-compliant increase in location-specific review velocity.

diagnostics.diagnosis: Review response coverage is below the governed operating target.
root_cause_hypotheses: No owner or response timeframe is defined.
The unanswered-review backlog is not reviewed consistently.
evidence_requirements: Count only reviews and responses available from supported providers.
Keep location and provider scope explicit.
Describe the target as an internal service level.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: Higher response coverage with accurate, approved responses.

diagnostics.diagnosis: The location's review footprint or pace trails a verified local comparison set.
root_cause_hypotheses: Competitors may have more consistent review-request operations.
The comparison set or collection window may not be equivalent.
evidence_requirements: Use the same location, category, provider, and capture date.
Require a named competitor set.
Do not infer ranking causality from review counts alone.
diagnostics.expected_outcome: The location narrows the verified review gap through compliant operations.

diagnostics.diagnosis: Required competitor facts are absent, stale, or below coverage requirements.
root_cause_hypotheses: The provider connection may be unavailable.
The selected competitors or locations may not be configured.
